summary.title: Qwen-UI-Agent Technical Report: Toward Next-Generation Real-World Centric Foundation GUI Agents

setting_and_object.category: System (foundation GUI-agent model plus its environment, data, training, and harness infrastructure)

details: GUI agents are largely optimized for simulated benchmarks and fail on real devices, in isolated single-platform domains, with GUI-only step-by-step actions and short horizons.
Building new agent capabilities still relies on human-intensive task construction, data collection, and failure analysis.
Qwen-UI-Agent: a real-world-centric foundation GUI agent spanning mobile, computer, browser, and DeepSearch, co-designed with its environments, data flywheel, RL training, and harness.
Unified action space that interleaves GUI operations with bash CLI execution and emits batched multi-action outputs in a single model turn.

Real-device mobile runtime (100+ physical phones, 150+ apps) used for task design, trajectory collection, online RL, and evaluation; an AutoResearch-style agent-driven flywheel constructs tasks/environments, diagnoses failures, and plans the next iteration; verifier-guided online RL over >100-turn trajectories with ~10,000 concurrent environments; a harness layer for proactive notification-triggered service and stateful cross-device workflows.
Three variants: 27B (primary), 35B-A3B (MoE, 3B active per token), 4B; initialized from Qwen base checkpoints (Qwen3.5-27B as base reference).
Training pipeline combines SFT, step-level 'action RL', and trajectory-level online RL with a model-adaptive curriculum that prioritizes intermediate-difficulty tasks.

MobileWorld-Real: 409 human-written everyday tasks over 104 apps in the Chinese mobile ecosystem, 7 domains, ~half labeled hard; run on live Android devices with real accounts, dynamic content, pop-ups, CAPTCHAs, expired logins; tasks requiring ask_user/user takeover; tasks and trajectories held out from training.

AutoJudge: trajectory-level evaluation by five independent VLM judges (majority vote) labeling pass / failed / env_error; env errors excluded from the success-rate denominator; validated against expert annotation on 666 trajectories.
Mobile: MobileWorld (GUI-only subset, 50-step and 100-step budgets), MobileWorld-Real, AndroidDaily.
Computer/browser/search: OSWorld-Verified (361 tasks), OSWorld-v2 (partial + binary), WebArena (with manually corrected reference answers and scripts), BrowseComp, BrowseComp-ZH.
Grounding: ScreenSpot-Pro (with/without zoom-in), ScreenSpot-V2, MMBench-GUI L2, OSWorld-G-Refined, UI-Vision.

General/agentic retention: MMMU-Pro, MMLU-Pro, MathVision, IFEval, Tau2-Bench, Terminal-Bench 2.0, Claw-Eval, BFCL-v4, SkillsBench, QwenClawBench (reproduced in-house with specified judges/simulators).
Frontier proprietary models: Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.6 Sol / GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Gemini 3.5 Flash, Seed 2.1 Pro.
Open-weight foundation models: Qwen 3.7 Plus, Kimi K2.6, MiniMax M3, Qwen3.5-27B (own base).
Specialized GUI agents: GUI-Owl-1.5-32B, UI-Venus-1.5-30B-A3B, UI-TARS-2, EvoCUA-32B, OpenCUA-72B, CUA-GYM-A17B.
Manual review of all failed Qwen 3.7 Plus trajectories on MobileWorld-Real and AndroidDaily to build a real-device failure taxonomy.
Action-level statistics of CLI share, batch share, batch size, and batch composition on OSWorld-Verified/v2.

Before/after comparisons for action RL (five error-pattern-specific test sets; frequent vs long-tail action rewards) and for online RL (verification rate, false-stop rate, modality mixing, constraint satisfaction).

key_findings.finding: The agent sets state of the art on real-device and simulated mobile use, beating frontier proprietary models at 27B scale.
key_findings.evidence: 92.2% on MobileWorld-Real (vs Seed 2.1 Pro 88.7%, Gemini 3.1 Pro 86.2%, GPT-5.6 Sol 85.4%, Opus 4.8 ~84.7%), 97.5% on AndroidDaily (vs 95.2% Seed 2.1 Pro), and 82.1% on MobileWorld under a 50-step budget (85.5% at 100 steps), exceeding GPT-5.6 Sol/Opus 4.8/Seed 2.1 Pro by 12.0/14.6/8.9 points and the best specialized GUI baseline (GUI-Owl-1.5-32B, 43.9%) by 38.2 points.

key_findings.finding: A unified GUI+CLI action space with batched outputs makes CLI a co-primary execution channel and shortens long-horizon computer-use trajectories.
key_findings.evidence: CLI accounts for 40.7% of actions in 92.0% of OSWorld-Verified tasks and 55.1% in 98.2% of OSWorld-v2 tasks; batched actions are 39.6%/41.6% of actions (3.1 primitives per batch); results are 79.5% on OSWorld-Verified (second overall, above GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Seed 2.1 Pro) and 40.0% partial / 13.9% binary on OSWorld-v2 with only 135.8 steps per task, i.e. +17.7 and +18.5 partial points over MiniMax M3 and Qwen 3.7 Plus while using 58.4% and 21.7% fewer steps.

key_findings.finding: Real-device failures of a strong frontier model decompose into a specific taxonomy dominated by realistic interface phenomena and weak error recovery, quantifying the simulation-to-real gap.
key_findings.evidence: Manual review of all failed Qwen 3.7 Plus trajectories attributes 52.0% of failures to real-world scenario challenges (UI misreading 24.7%, pop-up interference 18.2%, physical widget control 9.1%) and 40.3% to execution capability limitations (exploration failure 19.5%, erroneous action loops 14.3%, lost execution state 6.5%).

key_findings.finding: Online RL induces emergent verification and cross-modal division of labor (CLI to act, GUI to check) plus better long-horizon constraint adherence.
key_findings.evidence: On OSWorld, trajectories containing at least one verification action rise by 14.7% with an 11.2% drop in false-stop rate; GUI action share rises 6% and trajectories using both GUI and Bash rise 10.6%, with execution-then-GUI-inspection transitions increasing from 40.2% to 52.4%; full-constraint satisfaction rises 8.6% on OSWorld and 7.5% on BrowseComp-ZH.

key_findings.finding: Step-level action RL systematically corrects recurring action errors, especially short-range loops and rarely used actions, while reducing redundant reasoning.
key_findings.evidence: Overall task success improves by >7% with 21.3% fewer reasoning tokens and 8.4% more interaction steps; success rises on all five error-pattern test sets (repetitive action loops 72.9%->82.4%, confusable-element grounding 72.8%->79.1%, others +3.8 to +5.2 points); raising long-tail actions (e.g. ask_user, long_press, originally 19.9% of primitives) to ~40% of training data lifts their reward from 71.5% to 77.9%.
